title: acre-gui opens neovim on its drawing and links to it
body:
neovim starts the viewer and talks to it over the viewer's stdin and stdout, so a viewer opened on its own cannot be linked.

## Proposal

- acre-gui listens on a socket under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. A command in the viewer, "Edit in neovim", opens neovim on the active drawing with the socket's path passed on, and the plugin connects with `sockconnect` instead of starting a viewer. The messages stay the same.
- Outside decade the terminal comes from `xdg-terminal-exec`. Inside decade, neovim opens in decade's default terminal in a pane split beside the viewer, as `:AcreView` from neovim splits a pane for the viewer.
close_reason: Landed in 0237012. Without `--stdio`, acre-gui listens on `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/acre/<pid>.sock` (`Link::listen` in `link.rs`) and goes back to watching files when the editor disconnects. File > Edit in neovim runs the command from `neovim::command`. Outside decade that is `xdg-terminal-exec nvim FILE`. Inside decade it is ghostty with decade's flags and with `DECADE_PANE` and `DECADE_INTO` removed, so decade splits the focused pane. The plugin connects with `sockconnect` when `ACRE_SOCKET` is set. Nobody has tried it in a window yet.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/0c799e42
notes.text: Jack tried File > Edit in neovim by hand inside decade on 2026-11-24 at 5fc897c, once his neovim config gave the acre plugin its own lazy.nvim name, and it worked: neovim opened in a split beside the viewer and linked over the socket.
